There are some new obviously off topic messages in <#826479341784662056> <@552133098075193354> the same applies to <#749160974506000444> which I just posted a test message and deleted it Yeah, there's something weird where I can't stop people from posting... let me see again that is wierd OK we need an admin (vs. a mod) to do it. Pinged them. Could someone explain why mining nodes (seemingly) only consider gas for the next nonce rather than total gas of an EOA's TX queue? [This TX queue](https://etherscan.io/address/0x23983ea2123d40eb5655dfff3f3c917c78f214f6) seems beneficial to include in a block; two 100,000gwei TXes from yesterday are being held back by several sub-50gwei TXes from two days ago. It’s just harder for nodes to compute this than on, say, Bitcoin The earliest tx in that pending queue is not eligible for inclusion, and has not been for the last two days ( https://etherscan.io/tx/0xe5f978ffaccd6c77c487a923c9e6d775ad454a92c993a16d0fdb97c0ca529697 ). Its gas price is 23.31 Gwei, and the base fee hasn't gone that low from what I can tell. what happens if previous tx invalidates the next one? this could lead to dos attacks on block building although as there's no eth pull mechanism it could be included by assuming all previous tx spend all their msg.value (no refunds) <:peepothink2:754852084121206824>

excerpts.author: pietjepuk
excerpts.content:
The earliest tx in that pending queue is not eligible for inclusion, and has not been for the last two days ( https://etherscan.io/tx/0xe5f978ffaccd6c77c487a923c9e6d775ad454a92c993a16d0fdb97c0ca529697 ).
Its gas price is 23.31 Gwei, and the base fee hasn't gone that low from what I can tell.
